organizations.name: RCSB
organizations.summary: Research Collaboratory for Structural Bioinformatics, the US site of the worldwide Protein Data Bank.

organizations.name: EMBL-EBI
organizations.summary: European Bioinformatics Institute. Hosts PDBe, EMDB, AlphaFold DB and the BioImage Archive.

organizations.name: PDBj
organizations.summary: Protein Data Bank Japan, the Asian site of the worldwide Protein Data Bank.

organizations.name: Google DeepMind
organizations.summary: Research lab that developed AlphaFold and releases its predictions with EMBL-EBI.

organizations.name: EvolutionaryScale
organizations.summary: Organization behind the ESM protein language models and the ESM Atlas.

organizations.name: SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics
organizations.summary: Swiss bioinformatics institute that maintains SWISS-MODEL, ModelArchive and ExPASy.

organizations.name: NCBI
organizations.summary: US National Center for Biotechnology Information, part of the National Library of Medicine.

organizations.name: National Institutes of Health
organizations.summary: US National Institutes of Health.

organizations.name: National Library of Medicine
organizations.summary: US National Library of Medicine, which released the Visible Human Project.

organizations.name: National Cancer Institute
organizations.summary: US National Cancer Institute, which hosts The Cancer Imaging Archive and the Imaging Data Commons.

organizations.name: Scripps Research
organizations.summary: Research institute that maintains VIPERdb and cellPACK.

organizations.name: HHMI Janelia
organizations.summary: Howard Hughes Medical Institute campus for imaging, connectomics and cell biology.

organizations.name: Allen Institute
organizations.summary: Nonprofit research organization behind the Allen Brain Map, Allen Cell Explorer and related atlases.

organizations.name: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative
organizations.summary: Philanthropy that funds the CryoET Data Portal.

organizations.name: EPFL
organizations.summary: École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne, home of the Blue Brain Project.

organizations.name: Princeton University
organizations.summary: University that led the FlyWire reconstruction of the adult fruit-fly brain.

organizations.name: Harvard University
organizations.summary: University whose Lichtman lab released the H01 cubic millimeter of human cortex.

organizations.name: George Mason University
organizations.summary: University that maintains NeuroMorpho.Org.

organizations.name: Albert Einstein College of Medicine
organizations.summary: Medical school that maintains WormAtlas and WormWiring.

organizations.name: OpenWorm
organizations.summary: Open project building a 3D model and simulation of C. elegans.

organizations.name: EBRAINS
organizations.summary: European research infrastructure for brain atlases, including BigBrain.

organizations.name: INCF
organizations.summary: International Neuroinformatics Coordinating Facility, which hosts the Scalable Brain Atlas.

organizations.name: Max Planck Institute for Biological Intelligence
organizations.summary: Max Planck institute whose Baier lab maintains the mapZebrain larval zebrafish atlas.

organizations.name: Johns Hopkins University
organizations.summary: University associated with BossDB, a host for volumetric electron-microscopy datasets.

organizations.name: Database Center for Life Science
organizations.summary: Japanese life-science database center that publishes BodyParts3D.

organizations.name: Leiden University Medical Center
organizations.summary: Medical center that publishes the open AnatomyTOOL human model.

organizations.name: Brigham and Women's Hospital
organizations.summary: Hospital whose Surgical Planning Laboratory publishes the Open Anatomy atlases.

organizations.name: ESRF
organizations.summary: European Synchrotron Radiation Facility, where Human Organ Atlas scans are acquired.

organizations.name: HuBMAP Consortium
organizations.summary: Human BioMolecular Atlas Program consortium mapping the healthy human body.

organizations.name: IT'IS Foundation
organizations.summary: Foundation that builds the Virtual Population of computational human body models.

organizations.name: University of Auckland
organizations.summary: University that hosts the Cardiac Atlas Project.

organizations.name: Duke University
organizations.summary: University that hosts MorphoSource.

organizations.name: Natural History Museum
organizations.summary: Natural History Museum in London, which hosts Phenome10K.

organizations.name: University of Texas at Austin
organizations.summary: University whose high-resolution X-ray CT facility produces the DigiMorph library.

organizations.name: Smithsonian Institution
organizations.summary: Institution whose 3D program publishes scans of natural-history specimens.

organizations.name: Amsterdam UMC
organizations.summary: Medical center that built the 3D Atlas of Human Embryology.

organizations.name: University of Edinburgh
organizations.summary: University that maintains the eMouseAtlas of mouse embryonic development.

organizations.name: University of Cambridge
organizations.summary: University that helps maintain Virtual Fly Brain.

organizations.name: BioDigital
organizations.summary: Company that publishes the BioDigital Human anatomy platform.

organizations.name: Zygote Media Group
organizations.summary: Company that publishes Zygote Body, the successor to Google Body.

organizations.name: Visible Body
organizations.summary: Company that publishes commercial 3D anatomy applications.

organizations.name: Elsevier
organizations.summary: Publisher of Complete Anatomy, formerly 3D4Medical.

organizations.name: 3D Organon
organizations.summary: Company that publishes the 3D Organon anatomy platform.

organizations.name: IMAIOS
organizations.summary: Company that publishes e-Anatomy and Vet-Anatomy.

organizations.name: Primal Pictures
organizations.summary: Publisher of a long-running commercial 3D anatomy library.

organizations.name: Embodi3D
organizations.summary: Community library of medical models derived from patient imaging.

organizations.name: Sketchfab
organizations.summary: Platform museums and educators use to publish interactive 3D models.

organizations.name: Wikimedia Foundation
organizations.summary: Foundation that hosts Wikimedia Commons, including open 3D anatomy and biology models.

organizations.name: Stanford University
organizations.summary: University whose Center for Reproducible Neuroscience operates OpenNeuro.

organizations.name: University of Dundee
organizations.summary: University that develops the Open Microscopy Environment and the Image Data Resource.

organizations.name: Weizmann Institute of Science
organizations.summary: Institute where Proteopedia was created.

organizations.name: University of Vienna
organizations.summary: University that hosts PalDat, the palynological database.

organizations.name: British Geological Survey
organizations.summary: Survey involved in publishing British fossil type specimens as 3D models.

organizations.name: University of Montpellier
organizations.summary: University associated with MorphoMuseuM, a journal of vertebrate 3D models.

organizations.name: Washington University in St. Louis
organizations.summary: University that leads the Human Connectome Project.

organizations.name: University of California San Diego
organizations.summary: University that hosts the Cell Image Library.

organizations.name: FaceBase Consortium
organizations.summary: Consortium sharing craniofacial development data, including 3D morphology.

organizations.name: GUDMAP Consortium
organizations.summary: Consortium mapping genitourinary development, including 3D anatomy.

organizations.name: LungMAP Consortium
organizations.summary: Consortium mapping lung development with imaging and spatial data.

collections.name: RCSB PDB
collections.summary: Experimental protein, nucleic-acid and complex structures from the Protein Data Bank, with a 3D viewer on every entry.

collections.name: PDBe
collections.summary: European portal on the same worldwide PDB archive, with assemblies, validation and the Mol* viewer.

collections.name: PDBj
collections.summary: Japanese portal on the worldwide PDB archive, including electron microscopy and NMR services.

collections.name: EMDB
collections.summary: Cryo-EM density maps and fitted models. Each entry has a 3D view.

collections.name: EMPIAR
collections.summary: Raw electron-microscopy images, tilt series and tomograms that sit behind EMDB maps.

collections.name: AlphaFold DB
collections.summary: Predicted protein structures covering UniProt, including proteomes for human and other widely studied organisms.

collections.name: ESM Atlas
collections.summary: Predicted structures for metagenomic proteins, including sequences with no close experimental relative.

collections.name: SWISS-MODEL Repository
collections.summary: Homology models for UniProt sequences, with experimental PDB structures mapped alongside them.

collections.name: ModelArchive
collections.summary: Deposited computational structure models that are not part of the Protein Data Bank.

collections.name: PubChem
collections.summary: 3D conformers of small molecules, drugs and metabolites.

collections.name: NCBI Structure
collections.summary: MMDB macromolecular structures in the iCn3D viewer, linked to sequences, chemicals and taxonomy.

collections.name: VIPERdb
collections.summary: Icosahedral virus capsids, with coordinates derived from PDB entries and capsid-specific views.

collections.name: PDB-101
collections.summary: Educational views of molecules, including Molecule of the Month scenes built from PDB entries.

collections.name: Proteopedia
collections.summary: Wiki of annotated macromolecular scenes. Each page embeds a live 3D view of a structure.

collections.name: Protein Ensemble Database
collections.summary: Ensembles of protein conformations, for cases where one static model is the wrong picture.

collections.name: OpenOrganelle
collections.summary: Whole-cell and tissue volumes from focused ion beam electron microscopy, with organelle segmentations you can browse in 3D.

collections.name: Allen Cell Explorer
collections.summary: 3D views of human induced pluripotent stem cells, tagged organelles and integrated cell models.

collections.name: cellPACK
collections.summary: Mesoscale models that pack molecular structures into cell geometry.

collections.name: CryoET Data Portal
collections.summary: Annotated cryo-electron tomograms of cells and macromolecules in their native context.

collections.name: Cell Image Library
collections.summary: Public cell images, including 3D datasets of cells, organelles and small organisms.

collections.name: Image Data Resource
collections.summary: Published biological image studies, many of them 3D light-microscopy volumes.

collections.name: BioImage Archive
collections.summary: Archive for biological images that do not fit a specialist database, including 3D volumes.

collections.name: NeuroMorpho.Org
collections.summary: Largest public archive of digitally reconstructed neurons and glia, still adding new reconstructions.

collections.name: Allen Brain Map
collections.summary: Reference atlases for mouse, human and developing brain, with 3D annotation spaces.

collections.name: EBRAINS Atlases
collections.summary: Human, macaque, rat and mouse brain atlases in one viewer, including BigBrain.

collections.name: BigBrain
collections.summary: A 20-micrometer 3D reconstruction of a human brain, explored through EBRAINS.

collections.name: Scalable Brain Atlas
collections.summary: Browser for many template brains and atlases across species, on one coordinate viewer.

collections.name: Blue Brain Cell Atlas
collections.summary: 3D positions and densities of neurons and glia across the mouse brain.

collections.name: MICrONS Explorer
collections.summary: Mouse visual cortex at electron-microscopy resolution, with reconstructed neurons and synapses.

collections.name: H01 human cortex
collections.summary: A cubic millimeter of human temporal cortex, reconstructed from serial electron microscopy.

collections.name: FlyWire Codex
collections.summary: Whole adult fruit-fly brain connectome, with proofread neurons and their synapses.

collections.name: Virtual Fly Brain
collections.summary: Drosophila neuroanatomy, neuron images and connectomics registered to template brains.

collections.name: neuPrint
collections.summary: Janelia fly connectomes, including the hemibrain, mushroom body and medulla columns.

collections.name: mapZebrain
collections.summary: Larval zebrafish brain atlas with region annotations, traced neurons and a whole-brain electron-microscopy volume.

collections.name: MouseLight
collections.summary: Complete single-neuron reconstructions spanning the mouse brain.

collections.name: BossDB
collections.summary: Host for large volumetric electron-microscopy connectomes, viewed in Neuroglancer.

collections.name: WormAtlas
collections.summary: C. elegans anatomy, including the nervous system, slides and wiring.

collections.name: WormWiring
collections.summary: Electron-microscopy reconstructions and synaptic wiring for C. elegans.

collections.name: OpenWorm
collections.summary: Open 3D model and simulation of C. elegans, including body and connectome browsers.

collections.name: NIH 3D
collections.summary: Thousands of bioscience and medical models for viewing and 3D printing: anatomy, molecules, pathogens and the 3D Pollen Library.

collections.name: Visible Human Project
collections.summary: Cryosection, CT and MRI of one male and one female cadaver. A public-domain source behind many later anatomy meshes.

collections.name: BodyParts3D
collections.summary: Labeled adult male organs as STL and VTK files, indexed to Foundational Model of Anatomy terms.

collections.name: AnatomyTOOL
collections.summary: Open human anatomy model and browser from Leiden University Medical Center.

collections.name: Open Anatomy
collections.summary: Downloadable anatomy atlases from Brigham and Women's Hospital, including brain and head and neck.

collections.name: Human Organ Atlas
collections.summary: Synchrotron scans of intact human organs, from whole-organ scale down to about a micrometer.

collections.name: Human Reference Atlas
collections.summary: 3D reference organs for the healthy human body, tied to HuBMAP cell data.

collections.name: HuBMAP Data Portal
collections.summary: Tissue maps across more than 30 organs, explored from the whole body down to individual samples.

collections.name: IT'IS Virtual Population
collections.summary: Computational whole-body models of men, women and children, built for dosimetry and simulation.

collections.name: Cardiac Atlas Project
collections.summary: 3D heart models and imaging cohorts for cardiac anatomy.

collections.name: LungMAP
collections.summary: Developing and adult lung, shared as imaging and spatial data rather than a mesh store.

collections.name: GUDMAP
collections.summary: Genitourinary development atlas, including 3D views of kidney and reproductive anatomy.

collections.name: FaceBase
collections.summary: Craniofacial development data, including 3D morphology of human and model-organism faces.

collections.name: Embodi3D
collections.summary: Community library of medical models, mostly segmented from patient CT and MRI, for viewing and printing.

collections.name: BioDigital Human
collections.summary: Interactive male, female and pediatric anatomy, plus disease models. The fullest commercial body explorer.

collections.name: Zygote Body
collections.summary: Browser anatomy model descended from Google Body. Basic exploration is free and the full tool set is paid.

collections.name: Visible Body
collections.summary: Commercial anatomy apps covering the human body, muscles, physiology and some animal anatomy.

collections.name: Complete Anatomy
collections.summary: Elsevier anatomy platform, formerly 3D4Medical, with detailed regional models for teaching.

collections.name: 3D Organon
collections.summary: Commercial anatomy models for education, including virtual reality.

collections.name: IMAIOS e-Anatomy
collections.summary: Cross-sectional and 3D human anatomy aimed at radiology. Vet-Anatomy covers animals.

collections.name: Primal Pictures
collections.summary: Long-running commercial 3D anatomy library used in university teaching licenses.

collections.name: 3D Atlas of Human Embryology
collections.summary: Interactive reconstructions of human embryos from Carnegie stages 7 to 23, built in Amsterdam.

collections.name: Anatomy Portal
collections.summary: Optical projection tomography of embryos. Zebrafish from 24 hours to adult, and quail from day 1 to day 15.

collections.name: eMouseAtlas
collections.summary: 3D mouse embryo atlas and gene-expression resource from the Edinburgh Mouse Atlas.

collections.name: Allen Developing Mouse Brain
collections.summary: 3D reference atlas of the developing mouse brain across ages.

collections.name: MorphoSource
collections.summary: The main archive for CT, MRI and surface meshes of biological specimens. Home of the openVertebrate scans.

collections.name: Phenome10K
collections.summary: Downloadable STL scans of biological and fossil specimens. Free for academic and educational use.

collections.name: DigiMorph
collections.summary: CT visualizations and STL files for living and extinct vertebrates, plus a growing set of invertebrates.

collections.name: MorphoMuseuM
collections.summary: Peer-reviewed journal of vertebrate 3D models, including type specimens and anatomical atlases.

collections.name: Aves 3D
collections.summary: Avian skeletal elements, including the Thirioux dodo skeletons. Many of the same models are on Sketchfab.

collections.name: GB3D Type Fossils
collections.summary: British fossil type specimens as photographs and downloadable surface models.

collections.name: Smithsonian 3D
collections.summary: Smithsonian scans, including natural-history specimens and fossils.

collections.name: MorphoBank
collections.summary: Morphological matrices with media. Some projects include 3D specimen files alongside images.

collections.name: PalDat
collections.summary: Pollen morphology reference. Most records are micrographs. Downloadable 3D pollen meshes live in the NIH 3D Pollen Library, which links back here.

collections.name: Sketchfab
collections.summary: The viewer museums actually use. Natural history museums and anatomy authors publish models you can turn in a browser. Downloads depend on each model.

collections.name: Wikimedia Commons
collections.summary: Open GLB and STL anatomy and biology models, many of them reusable under Creative Commons.

collections.name: Print marketplaces
collections.summary: Thingiverse, Printables, MyMiniFactory, Cults3D, CGTrader, TurboSquid and GrabCAD. Anatomy models are common and scientific provenance varies.

collections.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
collections.summary: De-identified CT, MRI and PET of human bodies and tumors. These are image volumes, not finished surface meshes.

collections.name: Imaging Data Commons
collections.summary: NCI cloud of cancer imaging, including DICOM collections that can be rendered in 3D.

collections.name: Human Connectome Project
collections.summary: High-resolution MRI and diffusion imaging of healthy adult human brains.

collections.name: OpenNeuro
collections.summary: Public neuroimaging datasets, mostly MRI, shared by labs rather than as finished anatomy models.
